Electrons and photons also give rise to the functionality of the semiconductor materials that underpin our modern technology. The course includes a laboratory program relating to and supplementing the lecture material.
ZPEM2502.raw_requirements: Prerequisite: ZPEM1301 or ZPEM1303, ZPEM1302 or ZPEM1304, ZPEM1501 or ZPEM1503, ZPEM1502 or ZPEM1504, ZPEM2302 or ZPEM2309

ZPEM2506.title: Physics 2A: Meteorology and Atmospheric Physics
ZPEM2506.description: In this course we investigate the fundamentals of atmospheric physics and meteorology. Topics covered include: hydrostatic balance and the vertical structure of the atmosphere; altimetry; thermodynamics of dry and moist air; stability; cloud formation and precipitation; geostrophic, gradient and ageostrophic balances; winds; synoptic scale weather systems, air masses and fronts; radiation and the general circulation of the atmosphere; boundary layer processes. Material will be illustrated with applications from areas such as aviation, the marine and land environments, and our everyday experience of weather. The course includes a laboratory program relating to, and supplementing the lecture material.
ZPEM2506.raw_requirements: ZPEM1301 or ZPEM1303, ZPEM1302 or ZPEM1304, ZPEM1501.

ZPEM2508.title: Chemical, Biological, Radiological, Nuclear, Explosives
ZPEM2508.description: Weapons based on chemical, biological, radiological and nuclear agents have become an ever-present threat. Since the technology to produce such agents may now be available to many countries and possibly also to terrorist organisations, civil and military defence personnel need to be prepared to protect from such threats. This upper level, 6 UoC course introduces students to the scientific basis of chemical, biological, radiological and nuclear weapons (WMDs). Drawing on expertise from several academic staff and guest lecturers, the course has been designed to suit both engineering and science students. Students of this course will apply foundation knowledge in mathematics and science to advance their professional development in a field that is particularly relevant to their careers in Defence.

ZPEM2509.title: Astrophysics
ZPEM2509.description: The course objective is to provide both an introduction to modern astronomy and the theoretical and experimental physics that lies behind it. A broad range of topics are covered from celestial sphere coordinate systems to dark energy. This 6 UOC course is part of a Physics major in Science. It will be assumed that students have a good working knowledge from the foundation Physics 1 courses, ZPEM1501 and ZPEM1502, and that the student is proficient in Level 1 Mathematics.
ZPEM2509.raw_requirements: Prerequisite: ZPEM1301 or ZPEM1303, ZPEM1302 or ZPEM1304, ZPEM1501, ZPEM1502

ZPEM2901.title: Research Project 1
ZPEM2901.description: Students in the CDF Program will undertake one or more research-based projects together with coursework as set by the School. As one of the aims of the CDF program is to develop critical thinking and independent research skills, the projects will involve 'hands-on' research experience in collaborations with staff members and their research team. A supervisor, who is a member of academic staff, will work closely with the student and will manage each project. The project/s will be chosen after discussion between the student, the supervisor and possibly other members of staff.

ZPEM3103.title: Quantum Theory and Applications in Spectroscopy
ZPEM3103.description: Since the work of Isaac Newton, the development of quantum theory at the beginning of the 20th century was the greatest advance in physical science. Arguably, quantum mechanics has now become the most successful theory of all time. This course for upper level students of physics and chemistry presents a brief history of quantum theory, followed by an introduction to the standard formalism of quantum mechanics, e.g. the postulates of quantum theory, the properties of linear operators, Dirac notation etc. The gained knowledge is then applied to the physics of atoms and molecules and a range of spectroscopic methods, including electron spin resonance, nuclear magnetic resonance and rotational, vibrational and electronic spectroscopy.
ZPEM3103.raw_requirements: Prerequisite: ZPEM1301, ZPEM1302, ZPEM2113 or ZPEM2502

ZPEM3107.title: Explosives
ZPEM3107.description: Diverse aspects of explosives chemistry are covered, beginning with an introduction to explosive reactions and basic methods of estimating performance. Synthesis and properties of organic high explosives are discussed, and the relationship between structure and reactivity is explored. Various analytical detection methods are examined in the context of trace analysis of hidden explosives, including field methods, laboratory techniques and current research. The second part of the course concentrates on the physical processes occurring during initiation and explosion. Different methods for calculating detonation parameters and modelling explosive output are investigated. Factors affecting sensitivity are discussed, along with insensitive munitions.
ZPEM3107.raw_requirements: Prerequisite: ZPEM2102 and ZPEM2113, and declared Chemistry major (ACHMA1)

ZPEM3121.title: Supramolecular Chemistry
ZPEM3121.description: This course draws together concepts in inorganic, organic and some physical chemistry to study the behaviour and applications of supramolecular assemblies. Supramolecular Chemistry describes the chemistry of the interaction between discrete molecules and the collective properties of this interaction. Many supramolecular structures are found in the biological machinery of the cell and a number of emerging technologies employ molecular building blocks in the set of chemical applications now called nanotechnology.

ZPEM3202.title: Cultural Geography
ZPEM3202.description: Cultural geography is an important sub-discipline of human geography. Throughout the 1990s and 2000s it has been one of the discipline’s fastest growth areas. What do cultural geographers do and why has there been this rapid growth? This course explores these questions by examining the concept of conflict. We will use this examination of the changing nature of the concept of conflict to think through how different understandings of conflict create different mechanisms of inclusions and exclusion through three different spatial scales: territory (maps and geographic representations), borders (security and no-man zones), and bodies (desire and difference). In what ways do territory, borders and bodies relate to each other? And how do they define the idea and instance of conflict? Cultural geography approaches such questions by examining the way meaning is constructed differently according to differences in times, spaces and places.

ZPEM3204.title: Environmental Hazards
ZPEM3204.description: This course will look at both natural and human-induced environmental hazards and what their study can tell us about how humans interact with the environment. We will look at how a number of concepts (e.g. time/change; scale/intensity; risk/vulnerability) can inform our understanding of both hazards and institutional reactions thereto. As members of the ADF, it is quite likely at some point you will be involved in a relief operation either in Australia or overseas. An understanding of the nature of hazards, hazard mitigation and emergency management will help to prepare you for participation in these activities.

ZPEM3208.title: Geographic Research Methods
ZPEM3208.description:
Geography Research Methods is one of the more dynamic course offerings in Geography and it is compulsory to qualify for the Geography major (BA or Bsc). This course draws upon several of the theoretical and applied elements from the undergraduate geography program. Through lectures and group work, students are exposed to research frameworks in geography, topic definition, theory and methodology, practicalities of data collection, analysis and interpretation and report writing. The course provides students with experience in designing and undertaking a field-based geographic research project. The course normally involves a residential field school of approximately five days duration. 
Students are advised that this course requires self-directed study, and those students contemplating enrolling without having taken at least two third year geography courses are advised first to seek academic advice from the Geography discipline co-ordinator.

ZPEM3222.title: Coastal Geography
ZPEM3222.description: Australia has a very long coastline and more than 85% of our population is living along the coast. The coastal zone, where the land, sea and atmosphere meet, plays a fundamental role in human settlement, activity and development physically and economically. This course provides an introduction to coastal geography, which examines the development and evolution of coastal landforms and the processes which create and modify the coast. It deals with three components: coastal oceanography, sediment transport dynamics, and landform features. Special emphasis is given to the interaction and feedbacks between these three components plus human activities. Finally this course considers the response of the coastal zone to contemporary climate and sea-level changes and socio-economic development.

ZPEM3301.title: Topics in Mathematics
ZPEM3301.description: This course introduces a variety of topics in mathematics, including the historical development of mathematics. Topics may be selected from but not limited to the following: classical mechanics; data analysis; calculus of variations; complex variables; projectiles; optimization techniques; nonlinear dynamical systems theory; industrial mathematics; combinatorics; bush fire modelling; number theory.

ZPEM3306.title: Waves and Fluids
ZPEM3306.description:
Can the sea power our lives? This would provide a source of clean energy that will help address climate change. How can we make restaurants less noisy? This would certainly make dinner more pleasant. Are ultrasounds better with bubbles? Presently, it may be difficult to see how these questions are related.
In this course, we will look to understand waves, fluid dynamics, and understand the different behaviours of waves that are possible in fluids. Our questions are, perhaps surprisingly, all related to wave behaviour in fluids. We will examine ocean-wave energy conversion, acoustics, and medical applications of ultrasound microbubble contrast agents.
This course is designed to evoke your curiosity and cultivate a sense of motivation to foster your success in the course.
As we explore real world problems, we will develop idealized representations of these problems before we analyze them to find solutions. Importantly, these techniques are broadly applicable in many areas of academia, defence, and industry.

ZPEM3311.title: Mathematical Methods for Differential Equations
ZPEM3311.description: A variety of methods for solving ordinary and partial differential equations are considered. Examples and applications used to motivate the course will be drawn from areas such as solid and fluid mechanics, electrical circuits, pattern formation, heat and river pollution. The types of problems and methods of solution considered may include: systems of differential equations (including phase-plane analysis), boundary-value problems, partial differential equations and elementary perturbation analysis. Computational methods for solution of ordinary and partial differential equations will be introduced and software packages will be used to implement the algorithms and visualise the results.

ZPEM3313.title: Applied Nonlinear Dynamics
ZPEM3313.description:
Many nonlinear equations do not have explicit solutions. This course shifts the focus from finding explicit solutions to discovering geometric properties of solutions. It also recognises that even a small amount of nonlinearity in a physical system can be responsible for very complicated chaotic behaviour.
The fact that nonlinear systems do not guarantee regular or predictable behaviour is having a major impact on many fields of science and engineering, as well as mathematics. The discovery of chaos in simple dynamical systems changes our understanding of physical processes and has many practical applications including the understanding of the dynamics of the weather and climate, excitable media such as cardiac tissue and nerve fibres, population dynamics, transport in complex flow fields, to mention a few.
This course introduces the fundamentals of nonlinear dynamics with applications to physics, engineering, biology, and chemistry. It takes an intuitive approach with emphasis on geometric thinking, analytic and computational methods and makes extensive use of software packages, such as Matlab.

ZPEM3326.title: Time Series Analysis and Signal Processing
ZPEM3326.description:
Time series data (which are generated when measurements are taken over time) are widely used in many domains of applied science and engineering. This course provides students with skills that prepare them for working in areas such as oceanography and atmospheric science, econometrics, and signal processing applications, including analysis of radar, electro-optics, communications or information systems. 
The topics covered include the theory of time series; methods for analyzing trend and periodic variability in stationary and non-stationary time series; modelling with autocorrelation estimation; moving average processes; fitting an AR process; fitting an MA process; bivariate processes; Empirical mode decomposition and their applications.

ZPEM3401.title: Ocean Circulation and Mixing
ZPEM3401.description: This course examines the dynamics of large-scale wind-driven ocean currents. The course aims to explain why there is a broad equator-ward flow in all the major ocean basins, except the Southern Ocean, and why there are strong, poleward-flowing boundary currents such as the Gulf Stream and the East Australia Current on the western boundaries. The production of turbulence in the oceans and its role in mixing is also examined. The discussion of mixing in the ocean normally includes Kolmogoroff and Batchelor lengths, molecular mixing and diffusive boundary layers; the logarithmic boundary layer and mixing lengths; vertical mixing by wind and tidal stirring; dispersion in the ocean, its measurement, and the Taylor mechanism.

ZPEM3404.title: Ocean Waves and Modelling
ZPEM3404.description: This course covers ocean waves and modelling. Waves occur both on the surface of the ocean and within the ocean interior. Internal waves are important in mixing and sonar operations. After reviewing the basic principles of surface waves, this course presents the basics of internal waves, examining the dynamics, generation, propagation, and their impact on the ocean environment. Ocean modelling is a key component both in climate studies and naval operations. Basic modelling principles will be covered for both analytical and numerical ocean models with application to examples such as small-scale coastal systems, tsunamis, and the global ocean circulation.

ZPEM3503.title: Advanced Materials
ZPEM3503.description: The first part of the course is concerned with the propagation and interaction of electromagnetic radiation as employed in remote sensing situations. Even before it reaches the antenna the radiation must pass through cables and waveguides, and this also involves propagation and interaction. Fundamental to all of this are Maxwell's equations and an understanding of what they can tell us. The second part of the course provides an introduction to advanced materials with an emphasis on their structural and magnetic properties. The various structural states and phase diagrams are considered in terms of microstructure and its influence on mechanical properties. Finally, the basic theories of magnetism and the different types of magnetic materials are described and the use of modern magnetic materials is discussed with particular reference to permanent magnets, transformers, and data storage.

ZPEM3528.title: Nuclear Physics
ZPEM3528.description: Nuclear and particle physics in the big bang and in stars are responsible for the very character of our natural environment. Furthermore many modern technologies are based on subatomic physics. Examples can be found in the areas of power generation, medical diagnostics and treatment, industrial processing and control, as well as in environmental protection. In this course important aspects of nuclear and particle physics and their applications are discussed.

ZPEM3532.title: Advanced Topics in Physics and Oceanography
ZPEM3532.description: ZPEM3532 Advanced Topics in Physics and Oceanography is a compulsory component of Physics or Oceanography majors at UNSW Canberra and is designed to be equally applicable to students of either sub-discipline. It may also be offered as an elective to other Science students. The course provides a unique opportunity for students to build research skills relevant to their discipline, and affords the opportunity to apply some of the knowledge they have developed during the first two and a half years of their respective programs towards a directed research project in either Physics or Oceanography.

ZPEM3901.title: Research Project 2
ZPEM3901.description: Students in the CDF Program will undertake one or more research-based projects together with coursework as set by the School. As one of the aims of the CDF program is to develop critical thinking and independent research skills, the projects will involve 'hands-on' research experience in collaboration with staff members and their research teams. A supervisor, who is a member of academic staff, will work closely with the student and will manage each project. The project will be chosen after discussion between the student, the supervisor and possibly other members of staff .

ZPEM3902.title: Research Project 3
ZPEM3902.description: Students in the CDF Program will undertake one or more research-based projects together with coursework as set by the School. As one of the aims of the CDF program is to develop critical thinking and independent research skills, the projects will involve 'hands-on' research experience in collaboration with staff members and their research teams. A supervisor, who is a member of academic staff, will work closely with the student and will manage each project. The project will be chosen after discussion between the student, the supervisor and possibly other members of staff.

ZPEM4001.title: Science Honours Research 1
ZPEM4001.description: This 12UOC research course comprises part of the research component of all streams in 4513 Science (Honours) and also comprises part of the research component of the ZHSSGH Geography stream in 4511 Arts (Honours).

ZPEM4002.title: Science Honours Research 2
ZPEM4002.description: This 24UOC research course comprises part of the research component of all streams in 4513 Science (Honours) and also comprises part of the research component of the ZHSSGH Geography stream in 4511 Arts (Honours).

ZPEM4003.title: Science Honours Research 3
ZPEM4003.description: This 18UOC research course comprises part of the research component of all streams in 4513 Science (Honours) and also comprises part of the research component of the ZHSSGH Geography stream in 4511 Arts (Honours).

ZPEM4004.title: Science Honours Research 4
ZPEM4004.description: This 6 UoC research course comprises part of the research component of all streams in 4513 Science (Honours) and also comprises part of the research component of the ZHSSGH Human Geography stream in 4511 Arts (Honours).

ZPEM4101.description:

ZSPS1110.title: Cyber Crime and Ethics
ZSPS1110.description: Ethical and professional behaviour are the cornerstone of cybersecurity. This course provides students with fundamental ethical frameworks, applied to the cybersecurity profession. Students analyse topics and current and historic cyber events from ethical, professional, and legal perspectives. It also seeks to understand how computers and computing have created opportunities for crime and to analyse how they operate.The course equips students to recognise, effectively analyse, and respond to future ethical challenges as they arise, and to recognise new forms of criminal activity online.

ZSPS1111.title: Introduction to Information Technology and Networking
ZSPS1111.description:
Introduction to IT & Networking provides students with a broad foundation of modern information technology systems that form the key components of most of today's information systems. The course introduces key concepts in computer hardware, operating systems, and networking.
Through a mix of theory and practical lab work, students will learn the core functionalities of popular operating systems and will be provided with hands-on experience in navigating, configuring, and administering them using both graphical and command-line interfaces.
Students will also develop a solid understanding of how core IT systems support the transmission and sharing of information between digital devices across networks and the Internet using intermediary hardware devices and networking protocols.

ZSPS1112.title: Programming Fundamentals
ZSPS1112.description: This course develops the essential skills to write code that is not only correct but also readable and maintainable. Through hands-on exercises and practical examples, this teaches the fundamentals of a high-level programming language, enabling students to express ideas effectively and efficiently in code. This is the first introductory programming course, teaching the fundamentals of how programs are created, fundamental programming requirements, and initial concepts. This is a foundational block for future software development courses.

ZSPS1113.title: Computer Architecture and Operating Systems
ZSPS1113.description: This course is designed to provide students with a solid understanding of the essential concepts and components that form modern computation, with a focus on the physical components, firmware, and operating systems. Specifically, this course provides an understanding of the underlying operating systems which students have implicitly relied upon when developing applications in other courses and will serve to provide practical outcomes for their future careers. This course also takes a security-specific lens for operating system functions and limitations.
ZSPS1113.raw_requirements: Prerequisite: ZSPS1111 Introduction to Information Technology & Networking

ZSPS1337.title: Introduction to Cyber Security
ZSPS1337.description: Cyber security is headline news and a growing challenge for national and global security, while computer technology now pervades every aspect of the personal and professional lives of our graduates. This technology underpins enormous performance improvements but also brings serious vulnerabilities. This course provides an in-depth introduction to the foundational concepts of cyber security.This introductory course aims to provide a comprehensive understanding of the fundamental concepts and principles of cyber security, exploring the various cyber threats and vulnerabilities that exist in the digital landscape. This course explores the importance of raising awareness and educating users about cyber security best practices, emphasizing the role individuals play in ensuring a secure digital environment.

ZSPS2110.title: Data Structures & Algorithmic Knowledge
ZSPS2110.description:
The primary objective of this course is to enhance student comprehension of data structures and algorithms, to understand their theoretical complexity, practical behaviour, and their effective utilisation in the design of software systems.
The aim of this course is for students to become proficient programmers, equipped with knowledge of essential data structures and programming techniques. Students will be capable of constructing complex substantial software systems within a team environment, employing efficient data structures, widely used algorithms and sound programming practices.
The concepts taught in this course apply to all programming languages and software development domains and will lay a solid foundation for further specialised studies in computing, empowering students to delve into more advanced areas.

ZSPS2111.title: Knowledge Representation and Databases
ZSPS2111.description:
In today's technology-driven landscape, the indispensability of large data resources in every significant modern computer application cannot be overstated. Consequently, possessing the expertise to effectively understand and manage these resources is important.This course aims to explore in depth the practice of developing database applications and the theory behind large data storage systems and models, including relational database management systems (RDBMSs), NoSQL, Graph, and Map Reduce paradigms.
This course will equip students with the skills necessary to construct high-quality applications that exhibit correctness, efficiency, and usability, leveraging the potential of different storage paradigms. By engaging in comprehensive learning modules and hands-on exercises, students will develop a solid grasp of the fundamental principles and best practices required to build applications reliant on large data storage.

ZSPS2112.title: Web Application and Security
ZSPS2112.description:
This course covers the fundamentals of developing and securing web applications and websites.
Web applications are currently the major source of system vulnerabilities breached by complex cyber-attacks. This course will delve into the development of web applications and their security practices and standards. Students will learn web application vulnerabilities, and their exploitation and application security testing, authentication and authorisation, as well as secure web deployment. Students will also learn common types of web threats and how to protect against them in real-world case studies.
Overall, the course aims to educate students on best practices for developing secure web applications and protecting them from potential cyber threats.

ZSPS2113.title: Ethical Hacking & Penetration Testing
ZSPS2113.description: In this course, students will delve into the dynamic and rapidly evolving field of penetration testing. This process involves systematically identifying vulnerabilities in computer systems and networks to enhance their security. Through a blend of theoretical knowledge, practical exercises, and real-world case studies, students will develop the skills and mindset needed to become proficient ethical hackers.By the end of this course, students will have a strong foundation in ethical hacking methodologies and techniques. They will be able to identify and exploit vulnerabilities, conduct thorough penetration tests, and provide actionable recommendations to enhance system and network security. Additionally, students will understand the legal and ethical considerations associated with ethical hacking, empowering them to apply their skills responsibly and ethically in a professional setting.

ZSPS2114.title: Cyber Defence
ZSPS2114.description:
In this course, students will gain both a solid theoretical foundation and practical technical skills necessary for protecting contemporary systems and networks from potential attacks.
The course offers a comprehensive overview of modern attack techniques and explores a range of defensive measures and tools, highlighting their strengths and limitations.
The course aims to equip students with the technical expertise required to design and implement robust security measures in modern systems and networks.
Through hands-on exercises and real-world case studies, students will develop the practical skills and knowledge needed to identify vulnerabilities, assess risks, and implement effective security solutions to safeguard critical systems and networks.
Overall, the course provides the foundational knowledge of cyber defence and develops skills in applying various defence techniques, procedures, and tools.

ZSPS2115.title: Computational Mathematics and Applied Cryptography
ZSPS2115.description:
Mathematics is a key enabler of computer science and cyber security.
This course builds a foundation of mathematical concepts required by computing and cyber security graduates. The course includes foundation mathematics for computer science and cyber security and students learn various cryptographic techniques, including symmetric and asymmetric encryption, digital signatures and their applications such as blockchain.  
The course emphasises mathematical definitions and proofs as well as applicable methods as well as encompassing the fundamentals of cryptography and other applications.

ZSPS2116.title: Enterprise Cyber Security Governance and Policy
ZSPS2116.description:
This course provides a comprehensive understanding of the essential principles, frameworks, and practices involved in establishing effective cyber security governance and policy frameworks within organisations. In this course, students will explore the critical role of governance in ensuring cybersecurity resilience and compliance with relevant regulations and standards. They will also examine the formulation and implementation of cybersecurity policies to address emerging cyber threats and protect digital assets.
At the conclusion of this course, students will have a solid understanding of cybersecurity governance and policy principles, enabling them to develop and implement effective frameworks within organisations. They will be equipped to address regulatory requirements, mitigate cyber risks, and establish a culture of cyber security awareness and compliance.

ZSPS2117.title: Cyber Security Entrepreneurship
ZSPS2117.description:
The field of cybersecurity presents numerous opportunities for entrepreneurial ventures. This course aims to equip aspiring entrepreneurs with the knowledge, skills, and mindset required to navigate the intersection of cybersecurity and entrepreneurship. This course will provide students with the tools and insights necessary to thrive in the cybersecurity entrepreneurship space.
This course will teach students to identify market opportunities and develop innovative business ideas that address critical cybersecurity challenges. With a focus on entrepreneurial principles and frameworks, student will develop a robust business plan, considering market analysis, competitive positioning, revenue models, and growth strategies tailored specifically to the cybersecurity landscape. Understanding the legal, ethical, and regulatory considerations specific to cybersecurity entrepreneurship is paramount. This course builds on and extends work on data protection, privacy laws, intellectual property regulations, and ethical frameworks to ensure compliance and build trust with stakeholders.

ZSPS2118.title: Machine Learning for Cyber Security
ZSPS2118.description:
Existing cyber security solutions, such as firewalls, access controls, cyber threat intelligence and hunting, penetration testing, intrusion detection and prevention, and cryptography-based applications require automation and orchestration for achieving Intelligent Security in critical infrastructure systems and networks. Intelligent Security is a new trend in contemporary cyber security theories and practicals that develop artificial intelligence and machine learning for cyber security systems. This aims at devising intelligent methods for offensive and defensive applications, and the automation of the security processes to enhance efficiency and reduce human errors.
This course covers the fundamentals of machine learning theories, their practical implementation, and their utilisation in cyber security applications. Students learn data acquisition, exploration and visualisation techniques for cyber security industry challenges. Students also learn descriptive statistics and probabilistic models as the fundamentals of developing machine learning algorithms. Moreover, students practically learn supervised and unsupervised machine learning algorithms to solve red-blue teaming problems, along with industry standards and best practices.

ZSPS2119.title: Cyber Security Industry Project 1
ZSPS2119.description: This course prepares students with the necessary skills to effectively participate in work integrated learning projects, and the opportunity to apply learning from their programs to projects relevant to their career goals. Students will work with internal and in some instances, external mentors to identify project types, make project pitches, develop project ideas and understand execution processes as well as reflection.

ZSPS2121.title: Deep Learning for Cyber Security
ZSPS2121.description: This course covers theories and their practical implementation of deep learning for cyber security solutions. Deep learning is a subset of machine learning that involves the use of artificial neural networks to learn and make predictions based on large data sources. In the context of cyber security, deep learning models can be used to analyse vast amounts of data to build offensive and defensive strategies, such as automated penetration testing, intrusion discovery, vulnerability and malware detection in real-time. This can help organisations to understand how cyber threats would occur, detect and prevent them before they cause significant damage and achieve cyber resilience. Students learn discriminative and generative deep learning algorithms, Autoencoders, and convolution networks for various red-blue teaming scenarios from the industry perspective.
ZSPS2121.raw_requirements: Prerequisite: ZSPS2118 Machine Learning for Cyber Security

ZSPS2122.title: Trustworthy AI for Cyber Security
ZSPS2122.description:
This course covers advanced AI technology for cyber security, including explainable AI and adversarial machine learning algorithms. Trustworthy AI for cyber security involves the development of artificial intelligence systems that can operate securely and reliably in a variety of contexts. These systems are designed to detect and respond to various threats in cyberspace, such as malware, phishing attacks, and advanced persistent threats. To accomplish this, trustworthy AI incorporates a range of security measures, including encryption, secure communication channels, intrusion detection systems, and continuous monitoring and updating of threat intelligence, explanation and robustness of models. In addition, trustworthiness is also ensured through robust testing and validation processes that ensure the reliability and consistency of AI systems, and the identification and mitigation of potential biases or unintended consequences.
In this course, students learn the mitigation strategies against adversarial machine learning and consider the ramifications of deep fakes. Students also learn the implications of explainable AI and how to achieve responsible AI models for offensive and defensive problems.  Students will also learn the threats and mitigation for large language models (including GPT models), and their impact on cyber threat hunting and threat intelligence, and penetration testing.
ZSPS2122.raw_requirements: Prerequisite: ZSPS2118 Machine Learning for Cyber Security

ZSPS3110.title: Human-Centric Cyber Security
ZSPS3110.description:
This course covers a comprehensive approach to protecting and securing digital information and systems by focusing on the human component of the security equation.
The course introduces theoretical and practical aspects of behavioural analysis in cyber security, including an analysis of business models and criminological theories designed to modify behaviour and exploit human factors.
Students learn human behaviour as it relates to cyber security, especially the mental states of hackers and defenders. Students also learn the personality characteristics of victims, attackers and defenders, and with this knowledge, how policies, procedures and standards can be developed to reinforce an organisation's sustainability objectives.
ZSPS3110.raw_requirements:
Prerequisites: ZSPS1111 Introduction to Information Technology and Networking, and
ZSPS1337 Introduction to Cyber Security

ZSPS3111.title: Digital Forensics
ZSPS3111.description:
This course covers both the theory and practice of digital forensics. Students will learn to execute recent technologies of digital forensics in operating systems, and networks as well as implementing digital forensics principles using open-source digital forensic tools.
Students will also practice various digital forensic approaches, advanced learning-based forensics methods, and how they relate to incident response plans and professional reports that would be employed to be admissible as evidence in a court of law.
ZSPS3111.raw_requirements:
Prerequisites: ZSPS1111 Introduction to Information Technology and Networking, and
ZSPS1337 Introduction to Cyber Security

ZSPS3112.title: Internet of Things and Network Security
ZSPS3112.description:
The course covers security theory and technical aspects of Internet of Things (IoT) as well as associated network protocols and architectures. Topics include identifying common network attacks targeting IoT systems, analysing how these attacks occur, and applying effective countermeasures.
Students will design and implement technical controls across the OSI model to strengthen IoT network security. The course also introduces risk management strategies, intrusion detection and prevention techniques, and defensive measures against emerging threats to IoT environments. Overall, the course emphasises the secure integration of IoT devices into networks and examines relevant industry standards.

ZSPS3113.title: Cloud Computing and Security
ZSPS3113.description:
In today's rapidly evolving digital landscape, the cloud has become a fundamental component of modern computing. As organisations increasingly rely on cloud services to store, process, and manage their sensitive data, the need for robust cloud cyber security measures has never been more critical. In this course, students gain foundational knowledge of cloud computing, associated architectures and deployment models.
By the end of this course, students will have a comprehensive understanding of cloud cyber security principles, technologies, and best practices. Students will also be equipped to secure cloud environments effectively, mitigate risks, and protect sensitive data stored in the cloud.

ZSPS3114.title: Critical Infrastructure Protection
ZSPS3114.description:
Critical Infrastructure operations increasingly depend on the fourth revolution of Industry (Industry 4.0), including the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) and automated Industrial Control Systems (ICS). These systems comprise human-machine interfaces (HMI), programmable logic controllers (PLC), remote telemetry units (RTU), and supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) systems to offer smart critical infrastructure environments such as smart factories, smart healthcare, and smart grids. However, these systems suffer from various vulnerabilities and cyber attacks that attempt to compromise their critical infrastructure and achieve various attack motives.
This course covers the underpinnings of theories and practicals of critical infrastructure and their security controls. Students will learn the fundamentals of Industry 4.0 environments. The student then practices the vulnerabilities and threats against these environments. Finally, students learn the security controls and protection methods, including standards, policies and frameworks to protect critical infrastructure systems.

ZSPS3115.title: Advanced Ethical Hacking and Penetration Testing
ZSPS3115.description: The Advanced Ethical Hacking course is designed to deepen the knowledge and skills in the field of ethical hacking. This course goes beyond the fundamentals and focuses on advanced techniques and strategies used by cyber security experts to protect critical systems and networks. It seeks to focus on more complex, multistage attacks, and to give insight into different actions on objectives.

ZSPS3116.title: Cyber Risk Management & Incident Response
ZSPS3116.description: In today's technology-driven landscape, organisations face unprecedented challenges in protecting their valuable digital assets from cyber threats. Cyber risk management has emerged as a critical discipline that combines strategic planning, proactive risk assessment, and effective mitigation strategies to ensure the resilience of organisations against cyber threats. This course aims to equip students with the knowledge and skills necessary to navigate the complex world of cyber risk and develop robust risk management strategies. At the conclusion of this course, students will be equipped with the tools and techniques to assess and manage cyber risks, enabling them to make informed decisions to protect an organisation's digital assets.

ZSPS3118.title: Cyber Operations
ZSPS3118.description:
Cyber Operations develops the theoretical foundation and practical skills needed to design, implement and evaluate cyber operations within complex enterprise environments.  Students will explore both defensive and offensive security strategies used to protect, monitor and assess enterprise systems using best-practice frameworks, tools and operational processes.  The course equips students will skills and knowledge to analyse and respond to threats, simulate attacker behavior, and communicate operational insights to both technical and non-technical audiences.
Throughout this course students will gain insight into industry security roles and constructs such as SOC analysts, threat hunters, and red, blue and purple teams.  Defensive modules include techniques such as threat intelligence, monitoring and response aligned to enterprise operations and cyber resilience objectives.  Offensive modules focus on controlled and ethical activities including reconnaissance, scanning, exploitation and red team simulations used to assess and strengthen system security.
